title: Injective row descent implies descent for bounded-below injective complexes
statement: For X,R,W,U and the explicit restriction augmentation alpha [def-weil-pbc-proetale-hypercover-augmentation], assume every injective module sheaf I has a quasi-isomorphic row augmentation I(W)[0] to its alternating section row. Then alpha_J is a quasi-isomorphism for every strictly bounded-below termwise-injective complex J.

source.place: Tag 09A2, final paragraph, the injective-resolution row comparison

proof.text: Take K to be the flipped section bicomplex of J and A=J(W). The restriction maps form a:A to K.X 0, commute with coefficient differentials, and are killed by the next horizontal differential. K vanishes for p<0 or q below a lower bound for J, and A shares that bound.

For each coefficient degree identify the row map from the single-column bicomplex with the stated row augmentation, using singleMapHomologicalComplex and its degree-zero component. The remaining source components vanish. Apply bounded-below row augmentation comparison with b=alpha_J.
